rationale_summary: Breadth is very weak (positive asset share 16% over 5 sessions) with high cross-sectional dispersion (2.6%). I treat the deepest single-week drawdowns with strong prior trends (Taiwan, Korea, silver, copper, metals-mining) as overreaction candidates, while the crowded oil and cybersecurity spikes look like already-extended moves.
portfolio_rationale: Breadth collapse plus high dispersion into an FOMC week favors reversal in high-quality names that pulled back hardest against intact prior trends. Taiwan, South Korea, and silver combine top-quartile prior relative strength with extreme one-week relative pullbacks and plausible in-window catalysts, so they are ranked as overreaction with >55% probability. Extended winners (oil, cybersecurity, crypto) and structurally weak semis are ranked below the benchmark-equivalent threshold.

rationale_summary: SPY is down 1.2% over five sessions with only 16% of assets positive, a semiconductor-led shock (SOX -5.9% on Sept 14) and a broad breadth-negative tape. The FOMC decision on Sept 16 sits inside the window with the 10y at 4.97% and oil spiking to ~$106 Brent on a Saudi pipeline disruption; this is an event-driven, high-dispersion week where sharp one-week losers with intact prior trends (Taiwan, EM, South Africa, Korea, metals) offer the cleanest mean-reversion setups, while oil continuation is real but late and headline-dependent.
portfolio_rationale: Ranked the quality-pullback names highest: Taiwan, broad EM and South Africa each combine a strong prior relative trend with a sharp one-week relative drop, moderate drawdowns and no volume capitulation, consistent with temporary overreaction to the semiconductor and metals shock rather than deterioration. Korea and XME are similar but with far higher vol and beta, so they rank below despite similar mechanisms. Oil has genuine catalyst support but is extended and headline-path dependent; semis and cybersecurity lack quality support; crypto and munis are no-edge.
key_risks: FOMC decision Sept 16 with the 10y at 4.97% could drive a hawkish repricing that hits high-beta EM and Asian equities harder than SPY; Semiconductor selloff may continue, dragging Taiwan and Korea further regardless of prior trend; Oil above $105 from the Saudi pipeline disruption could either extend (hurting EM importers) or collapse if repaired, adding two-way volatility; Dollar strength (DXY 99.41, rising) pressures unhedged EM and South Africa returns; China data show weak retail sales and -19.9% real-estate investment, limiting EM demand tailwinds
